newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says EU tax rules must be applied uniformly.
newsitem.headline: Court says EU tax rules must be applied uniformly.

text.p: The European Court of Justice decided on Thursday lawyers benefitting from VAT exemptions in one member state are not entitled to a refund of VAT paid in another member state, according to Community VAT rules.

A Belgian lawyer, Etienne Debouche, leased a car in the Netherlands. The car was used exclusively for professional activity in Belgium and Debouche asked the Dutch authorities for a refund of the VAT he paid.

The Eighth VAT directive explicitly states that to qualify for a refund an individual must produce a certificate stating he is subject to VAT in his member state. Debouche produced a statement from Belgium that he was not subject to VAT in Belgium.
The court noted the Eighth directive is not meant to circumvent VAT rules under the Sixth VAT directive, but only to eliminate discrepancies between member states' rules.
The court said, "the Eighth directive must not lead to the treatment of taxable persons differing according to the member state in the territroy of which they are established."
The court noted that if Debouche were to receive the refund, he would receive better treatment than Dutch lawyers.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: Dutch)

"Value added tax - Interpretation of article 17(2) and (3)(a) of directive 77/388/EEC and of artricle 3(b) and the first paragraph of article 5 of directive 79/1072/EEC - Refund of value added tax to taxable persons not established in the territory of the country"
Reference by the Gerectshof, The Hague, for a preliminary ruling in the proceedings pending before that court between

on the interpretation of articles 17(2) and (3)(a) of the Sixth Council directive 77/388/EEC of 17 May 1977 on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment (OJ 1977 L 145, p. 1) and of article 3(b) and the first paragraph of article 5 of the Eighth Council directive 79/1072/EEC of 6 December 1979 on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Arrangements for the refund of value added tax to taxable persons not established in the territory of the country (OJ 1979 L 331, p. 11)

Article 3(b) and the first paragraph of article 5 of the Eighth Council directive (No 79/1072/EEC of 6 December 1979 on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Arrangements for the refund of value added tax to taxable persons not established in the territory of the country) is to be interpreted as meaning that the fact that a lawyer benefits, pursuant to article 28(3)(b) of the Sixth Council directive (No 77/388/EEC of 17 May 1977 on the harmonization of the laws of the member states relating to turnover taxes - Common system of value added tax: uniform basis of assessment) and Annex F thereto, from an exemption in the member state in which he is established does not entitle him to request the competent authorities of the member state to issue the certificate mentioned therein and he is not, accordingly, entitled to a refund of the VAT charged on services supplied to him in a member state in which he is not established and in whcih services supplied by lawyers are not exempted.
